match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the chord theorem: the perpendicular from the centre bisecting a chord and equal chords being equidistant from the centre. The bank cards cover calculus rates of change, enlargements, and circle and ellipse equations, which are unrelated.

draft.title: Chords and the centre
card: A chord is a straight line joining two points on a circle. The distance from the centre to a chord is measured along the perpendicular, the shortest path.
A line from the centre perpendicular to a chord cuts the chord in half. The same works backwards: a line from the centre to the midpoint of a chord meets it at \(90^{\circ}\).
Equal chords are the same distance from the centre. Chords that are the same distance from the centre are equal in length.
A circle has radius 13 cm. A chord is 5 cm from the centre. Half the chord is \(\sqrt{13^{2} - 5^{2}} = \sqrt{144} = 12\) cm, so the chord is 24 cm long.
draft.remember: Centre to chord at a right angle: it halves the chord. Equal chords sit equally far from the centre.

a.q: A line from the centre of a circle meets a chord at \(90^{\circ}\). The chord is 18 cm long. How far is the meeting point from one end of the chord?
a.why: A perpendicular from the centre cuts the chord in half, so each part is \(18 \div 2 = 9\) cm. Doubling to 36 cm is tempting, but the line halves the chord and does not double it.
a.clue: What does the perpendicular do to the chord?

b.q: A circle has radius 10 cm. A chord is 6 cm from the centre. How long is the chord?
b.why: Half the chord is \(\sqrt{10^{2} - 6^{2}} = \sqrt{64} = 8\) cm, so the whole chord is 16 cm. The answer 8 cm is the tempting one, but it is only half the chord.
b.clue: Find half the chord first, using a right-angled triangle with the radius as its longest side.

wants.brief: A circle with centre O and a chord AB. A line from O meets AB at point M with a right angle marked at M. Mark AM and MB as equal with matching tick marks.
wants.why: It shows the perpendicular from the centre halving the chord.
